title: PEI’s Ten Greatest Postcards
summary: Nine cards I can put on the table, and room for a tenth. Each image opens the story and its companion postcards.

title: Yours truly, Alice Maude Kinch
summary: A signed portrait, two Island family histories and an iceboat survivor’s own account take us from Cascumpec to a dentist’s family in Massachusetts.

title: Before the Farewell: The Island Prepares for War
summary: Armouries, horses, heavy guns, Niobe’s salute and letters from camp: the postcards that carry the Island from peacetime preparation into the First World War.

title: Carter’s Island in Amber
summary: Red captions, apricot skies and four different pictures of Rosebank under one name. An alphabetical gallery of 22 Carter views and one unsigned match.

title: The Church in the Picture: A Postcard Map of Island Communities
summary: Explore 62 church, chapel and convent views at 23 Island stops. A clickable map follows the buildings, the communities behind them, and the postcards that preserve what changed.

title: “Here Is a Pretty View for You”: Dalvay in 1901
summary: Effie sent a picture of a private summer house and news of market day to a friend in Massachusetts. Her oversized postcard is the earliest Island-postmarked view of P.E.I. in the collection.

title: Five Cents at Wonderland
summary: A sign over a Market Square doorway leads to a five-cent picture show in Charlottetown in 1907. Two newspaper clippings tell us what audiences saw and heard. Three postcard senders tell us what took them to the square.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #4 – Frank Snake in Two Summerside Postcards
summary: A pencilled name, two editions of one portrait, and three destinations. What the Summerside publishers printed and what the senders added.

title: From Board Ice to Board Ice
summary: Crossing the Strait by iceboat. Eleven postcard views, a two-dollar ticket and the memories of a passenger who wore the wrong shoes for the journey.

title: From Government House to G3MY: The QSL Cards of Prince Edward Island
summary: In 1958, Walter Hyndman crossed out his home address on a radio card and wrote “Government House.” Seven illustrated chapters follow the Island’s shortwave operators and distant listeners from 1927 to 1959.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #5 – A Christmas Card from One Chief to Another
summary: Chief Matthew Francis signed a Christmas greeting to a chief in Truro. A second Pictou portrait helps put names to people in the first.

title: From St. James to Senator Yeo’s Gate
summary: A red monument at Port Hill leads to three houses in the 1880 atlas, a shipbuilding family, and two men at a gate whom the photographer left unnamed.

title: J. A. S. Bayer, Charlottetown Photographer
summary: A Halifax photographer takes over an Island studio. His shop-window displays, fox trains, college portraits and a day at Stanhope trace a career from 1901 to 1928.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #8 – Largest Ever Caught on P.E. Island
summary: A 1911 message dates Pugh’s famous lobster picture. A factory view and a pair from Mount Stewart show what canning meant along the Island shore.

title: Lights Around the Island: A Lighthouse Postcard Map
summary: Explore lighthouse postcards from across the collection: working harbours, coastal towers and range lights, with a clickable map and the complete Kodak-paper album.

title: Looking for “Louson Photo”
summary: Two ways of signing an Island photograph. Browse the unnumbered views by caption and twelve “Louson Photo” views by the numbers on the prints.

title: Two Fairmiles and a Warehouse on the Montague Waterfront
summary: Two hull numbers lead to wartime rescues and two Montague owners. A warehouse sign and an earlier sender’s note recover the trade along the wharf.

title: The Montague Furnishing Company’s Casket Cards
summary: A labelled view of the Montague factory, a furniture order from 1900, and seven casket designs traced through the company’s advertising postcards.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #2 – The New Railway Station in Montague
summary: A ten-year wait for Montague’s first-train postcard, a morning timetable, Georgetown’s station sample and the steamer contract that served the same waterfront.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #10 – My Heart’s Desire
summary: The distance between my bid and the winning one was sixty-five cents. I’ve left a postcard-sized space for the copy I still hope to find.

title: A Little Island News for Mrs. Whidden
summary: An Alberton souvenir carried news of a burial, an ailing aunt and an offer of work to Shubenacadie. A family stone at North Bedeque may tell us who Mrs. Hooper was.

title: The DNA of P.E.I. Postcards, Part Three: Bayer’s Name in the Margin
summary: Nine signed photographs begin the search for a wider family of early Island postcards. Follow the unsigned companions, possible new views, and images that travelled into other publishers’ cards and a souvenir album.

title: The DNA of P.E.I. Postcards, Part Two: One Market, Several Names
summary: A Bayer credit, Haszard and Taylor postcards, and a Carter album supplied by Louson: the same Market Building photograph leads through several Island businesses. Four versions side by side, with the evidence and the unanswered questions kept distinct.

title: The DNA of P.E.I. Postcards, Part One: Pugh’s 524 Series
summary: Twenty-two numbered Charlottetown views, seven exact photographic matches, and the ghost lettering beneath the colour. Follow the images through Pugh’s 524 series, with spaces for the cards still to be found.

title: The Railway Stations of Prince Edward Island
summary: Choose a town on the October 1919 railway map. Eleven station albums take you from the locomotive at Tignish to Montague’s first train and the platform at Murray Harbour.

title: “Some of Our Near Neighbors” — Mi’kmaw Lives on Island Postcards
summary: A Christmas greeting from Richmond, Sally Mitchell’s name in an archival record, and a basket taking shape. Mi’kmaw lives come into view on both sides of these Island postcards.

title: “You Can Find Me Here Too”: The S.S. Anna at Montague
summary: Two cats, fourteen men and a note signed “R.” A Norwegian crew posed at Montague in 1913 while Island produce was being loaded for Havana.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #7 – The Night St. Dunstan’s Burned
summary: Four timed photographs, Walter Stiff’s Richmond Street imprint and a Cape Cod family trail. Pre-fire and rebuilt interiors show what the congregation lost and recovered.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #9 – The Card That Started My Collection
summary: A photograph of four men in a carriage led me to a newspaper portrait of W. Stetson Rogers and the story of the Odd Fellows gathering in Charlottetown in August 1908.

title: Looking West: The E.J.L. Postcards of Southeastern P.E.I.
summary: A rowboat at Murray Harbour and sails at Belle River lead to five consecutive E.J.L. designs, photographer Elliot Lumsden, and eight more Island views to compare.

title: The Horses in the Picture
summary: From a little girl at Souris to sleighs beside the Stanley: the horses that worked, travelled and quietly held their place in Island life.

title: The Island in the Post, 1877–1949
summary: Four charts and a map-reading puzzle from the postcard collection. Follow the surviving postmarks by year, month and town, from a bank cashier’s penny card to a summer at Dalvay.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #3 – The Million-Dollar Fox Train
summary: Bayer’s train portrait names three fox-industry men. A baggage master, a director’s signature and photographs from four Island ranches help explain the value of live breeding stock.

title: The Names They Left Us: Remembering the Island’s Fallen
summary: A Summerside unveiling, Charlottetown’s two soldiers’ monuments, O’Leary, Tignish and a nurse’s memorial hospital: postcards of the Island learning how to remember.

title: The Strait by Ferry
summary: Trace the two-ferry round trip on the 1941 ticket, then explore seven Strait crossings and fourteen ship albums, from Stanley and Minto to the original Abegweit.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #1 – The Tunnel
summary: A train hidden on the address side, an iceboat crossing between the same capes, and three senders with their own reasons to want a tunnel.

title: The View from the Minister’s Window
summary: Five Cardigan cards identify Edwin Smith’s waterfront photographs. A captain’s greeting, a Woodville message and a parishioner’s Sunday letter give them a life beyond the printer.

title: PEI’s Greatest Postcards – #6 – Troops Embarking at Charlottetown
summary: Island artillerymen and two gun barrels aboard the Cacouna. A second photograph, the ship’s reported load, and an August 3 family message place the departure in the first days of war.

title: “Hope We Have Got Rid of the Hoodoo”
summary: Engine trouble brought the Village Belle to Souris in August 1914. Six lines to Susan Knight, two newspaper clippings and a constable’s notebook follow an Arctic expedition from an Island wharf to Baker Lake and beyond.
